title: Hackers Drain $351.6 Million From Bitget Hot Wallets in Major Crypto Breach
content_md: Cryptocurrency exchange Bitget has confirmed that attackers siphoned approximately $351.6 million from parts of its hot- and warm-wallet environment, marking one of the largest exchange security incidents of 2026. The company said cold wallets were not affected and stated that customer account balances remain accurate while its security review continues. Bitget detected unauthorized transfers at 18:31 UTC on September 24, 2026, and activated emergency response procedures within minutes. The exchange has temporarily paused withdrawals, but deposits and trading remain operational. Hackers Drain $351.6 Million From Bitget Hot Wallets Bitget said it identified, flagged, and reported abnormal recipient addresses, and engaged law enforcement agencies and blockchain-security firms to trace the stolen funds. The breach affected only part of Bitget’s three-tier wallet architecture, specifically its hot- and warm-wallet layers. Hot wallets are internet-connected systems designed to support immediate transaction processing, while warm wallets generally provide a middle layer between online liquidity and fully offline cold storage. Before Bitget disclosed the full estimated exposure, on-chain observers had tracked suspicious transactions valued between roughly $174 million and $183 million. The final confirmed figure of $351.6 million suggests the attacker activity extended beyond the wallet movements initially visible to public blockchain analysts.
